content: Lactitol is a sugar alcohol that serves as a bulk sweetener in low-calorie foods, providing approximately 40% of the sweetness of regular sugar. It is also utilized in medical settings as a laxative. Lactitol is manufactured by two companies, Danisco and Purac Biochem. Lactitol is commonly used in various low-energy or low-fat food products. Its high stability makes it particularly suitable for baking. It is frequently found in sugar-free candies, cookies (biscuits), chocolate, and ice cream. Additionally, lactitol acts as a prebiotic, promoting colon health. It provides 4 calories (9 kilojoules) per gram, which is lower than the 4 calories (17 kilojoules) per gram typically found in carbohydrates. Lactitol is also used as an excipient in certain prescription medications, such as Adderall, and is marketed under the trade name Importal. When combined with ispaghula husk, lactitol is an approved treatment for idiopathic constipation, functioning as a laxative to prevent or manage constipation. Lactitol, along with other sugar alcohols such as erythritol, sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol, and maltitol, is classified by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as generally recognized as safe (GRAS). These sugar alcohols are approved as food additives and are known not to contribute to tooth decay or cause significant increases in blood glucose levels. Lactitol is approved for use in food products in most countries worldwide. However, like most sugar alcohols (with the exception of erythritol), lactitol can cause gastrointestinal side effects such as cramping, flatulence, and diarrhea in some individuals. This occurs because humans lack an appropriate beta-galactosidase enzyme in the upper gastrointestinal tract, resulting in most ingested lactitol reaching the large intestine. In the large intestine, lactitol becomes fermentable by gut microbes (acting as a prebiotic) and can draw water into the gut via osmosis. A human study involving lactitol-sweetened chocolate found that consuming 5 grams per day or less caused no gastrointestinal changes, while 10 grams per day caused minimal changes. Individuals with other health conditions are advised to consult their general practitioner or dietitian before consuming lactitol.
